transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me. It's very nice to meet you, too. 

I, um... well, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. I'm sure it's probably just me getting a bit older, but I've been having a little trouble at work. I'm a carpenter, and... well, it's a bit embarrassing to admit, but I just cannot seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. 

Like, if one saw starts up in the shop, or if somebody just walks past the office... or honestly, even if I just have a passing thought about a different job, it completely pulls me off what I’m doing. And then before I know it, the whole day just kind of gets away from me. I try really hard to stay on track, I really do, but... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you struggled with this inability to stay focused your entire life, or is this something that has only started happening more recently?

Oh, um... well, to be perfectly honest, it really hasn't been my whole life. At least, not this bad. This... this level of trouble has really only been going on for about a year and a month. 

You see, I had a bit of a clumsy moment and broke my wrist back then. Because I couldn't use my hands, they shifted me into doing the shop paperwork and supervising the crew instead of my usual hands-on carpentry. I'm so grateful they kept me on and accommodated me, I really am, but... I guess sitting at a desk doing forms instead of working with my hands is just when I really started noticing that I can't seem to keep my brain on track. 

I hope that answers your question okay? I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining about doing desk work, it's just... it's been a struggle. Am I explaining that alright?
Aside from the trouble focusing, have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless since you were moved to the desk job?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I mean, I wouldn't say I've been feeling hopeless or sad or anything like that. I'm actually a very positive person, usually. 

I know it probably sounds like I'm whining about the desk job, but I really am fine with it. I mean, I miss the tools, sure, but I'm just so thankful to have a job that takes care of me. I really don't want you to think I'm depressed or ungrateful. It's just... just this silly trouble keeping my mind on the paperwork. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression about how I feel.
Beyond the difficulty focusing on your paperwork, do you find that you spend a significant amount of your time feeling excessively worried or anxious about various things in your daily life?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I try really hard not to be a worrywart or anything like that. I'm usually pretty good at just taking things as they come. 

I mean, sure, I want to make sure I'm doing a good job for the crew, and I want to get the forms right so I don't cause any trouble for the boss, but... no, I wouldn't say I'm excessively anxious. I try to just stay positive and keep a smile on. 

I hope that's what you were asking? I just really don't want to make it sound like I'm falling apart or, you know, making a mountain out of a molehill. I'm doing okay in that department, I think. Is that a helpful answer?
Looking back at your childhood or your time in school, did you ever struggle with being easily distracted or having trouble staying on task back then?

Oh, um... well... I guess if I'm being completely honest, there might have been a little bit of that when I was younger. But I really don't want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or a troublemaker! I was actually a very sweet girl, I promise. 

It's just... well, even back in grade school, like, before I was 12, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was, um, bright but maybe a little careless? I guess I had a bad habit of losing my homework or forgetting what the teacher had just told us to do. And... well, they said I spent a lot of time staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. 

But I wasn't trying to be difficult, I swear! I just had a bit of a daydreaming habit, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a terrible student. I always tried my best to be good. Did I answer that okay for you?
